title: Intersection of the I-adic filtration of a finite module vanishes near V(I)
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $M$ a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $N=\bigcap_{n\ge0}I^nM$. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ there is $f\in R$, $f\notin\mathfrak p$, with $N_f=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], i.e. every element of $N$ is annihilated by some power of $f$. (Part (2) of the source, $N=0$ when $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical, is not stated here.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, line 12257), part (1); its proof uses Lemma Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic, line 12154) and Lemma Tag 00IP (lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero, line 12241)

proof.text: $N$ is finitely generated. $N=\bigcap_{n\ge0}I^nM$ is an $R$-submodule of the finitely generated $R$-module $M$ over the Noetherian ring $R$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] $N$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, line 12257) (1): 'Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be generators for the module $N$, see Lemma 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic, line 12154)'

proof.text: Krull's intersection theorem over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$ and put $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$. The localization $R_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}R$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so its Jacobson radical (the intersection of all maximal ideals) is $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, and $J:=IR_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ since $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] (with $R'=S^{-1}R$, $r\mapsto r/1$). The $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $M_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]: if $m_1,\dots,m_l$ generate $M$ and $m=\sum_ja_jm_j$, then $m/s=\sum_j(a_j/s)(m_j/1)$, so the $m_j/1$ generate. By [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] applied to $R_{\mathfrak p}$, $J$ and $M_{\mathfrak p}$, $\bigcap_{n\ge0}J^nM_{\mathfrak p}=0$. (This is Stacks Lemma 00IP for the Noetherian local ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and the proper ideal $J$.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, line 12257) (1): 'the image of $N$ in the localization $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is zero, by Lemma 00IP' (lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero, line 12241); $R_{\mathfrak p}$ Noetherian by Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence, line 5991), implicit in Stacks

proof.text: The image of $N$ in $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is zero. Let $x\in N$ and $n\ge0$. Since $x\in I^nM$, $x=\sum_ia_iy_i$ with $a_i\in I^n$, $y_i\in M$, and each $a_i$ is a sum of products $b_1\cdots b_n$ with $b_k\in I$; hence $x/1=\sum_i(a_i/1)(y_i/1)$ with $a_i/1=\sum(b_1/1)\cdots(b_n/1)\in J^n$, so $x/1\in J^nM_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus $x/1\in\bigcap_nJ^nM_{\mathfrak p}=0$ by step 2, and by the description of the kernel of the localization map in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] there is $t\in S$ with $tx=0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, line 12257) (1): 'we can find $g_i\in R$, $g_i\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $x_i$ maps to zero in $N_{g_i}$. Thus $N_{g_1g_2\ldots g_n}=0$'

proof.text: $N_f=0$. Every element of $N_f$ is $x/f^e$ with $x\in N$, $e\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]; since $f\cdot x=0$, $x/1=0$ (the criterion $f^kx=0$ with $k=1$), and $x/f^e=(1/f^e)(x/1)=0$. Equivalently every element of $N$ is annihilated by a power of $f$, namely $f$ itself.

Five steps following Stacks: N finitely generated (existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite, 00IK); Krull's intersection theorem 00IP over the Noetherian local ring R_p realized by the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson (Ideal.iInf_pow_smul_eq_bot_of_le_jacobson), since the Jacobson radical of R_p is pR_p which contains IR_p, with R_p Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian (00FN, implicit in Stacks) and M_p finite over R_p written out; image of N in M_p zero (elementary, I^nM maps into (IR_p)^nM_p); one f outside p killing N by the existing lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-localization-zero-annihilator (Stacks' product of the g_i); N_f=0 (elementary).
